% A KOMA-Script document's own \deffootnote, with a mark indent smaller
% than the text's, in scrbook with Times and hyperref: each footnote
% keeps the words and spaces of the PDF, whatever its first word's width. Also a
% footnote in a minipage.
\documentclass{scrbook}
\usepackage{times}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\deffootnote[0.5em]{2em}{1em}{\textsuperscript{\thefootnotemark}}
\begin{document}
\chapter{First}
Text one.\footnote{I thank a critic for this.}
Text two.\footnote{A measure is finite again.}
Text three.\footnote{We thank the binder too.}
Text four.\footnote{I am in debt to them.}
Text five.\footnote{It is so.}
Text six.\footnote{If so, then.}
Text seven.\footnote{Me too, then.}

\begin{minipage}{0.8\textwidth}
In a box.\footnote{I add this in a box.}
\end{minipage}
\end{document}
